newsitem.title: DENMARK: Danish bond prices slip in becalmed summer market.
newsitem.headline: Danish bond prices slip in becalmed summer market.

text.p: Danish bond prices slipped undramatically on Friday in a becalmed summer market, lulled by closed bourses abroad, with dealers predicting that the cautious, wait-and-see mood would prevail until the close.
"The market is very quiet, Germany and other exchanges are shut, I see the morning's slightly downward trend continuing until the close," one dealer said.

The benchmark eight percent state bond due 2006 was down 0.12 point from the opening at 112.52, yielding 6.08 percent with the seven percent 2007 bond, due to become benchmark on Sept 1, 0.15 point down at 105.41, with yield at 6.27 percent.
Turnover in the tone-setting 2006 and 2007 bonds was around400 and 250 million crowns respectively.
The 2006's September future rose 0.06 point to 112.32 with 31 contracts traded.
The six percent mortgage bond due 2026 gained 0.23 point to 91.35.
The crown traded at 3.8095 per mark at 1100 gmt, down a smidgen from around 3.8090 at the opening.
The 10-year yield gap with Germany narrowed two basis points to 58 bps.
